narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your savings account status, your employment situation, and the length of the loan you requested. Your lack of any known savings was the single biggest reason the application was turned down. Most approved applicants have at least some savings on record, whereas you fall into the unknown or no-savings group. This absence of a financial buffer pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your current unemployment also worked against you. Only about 7% of approved customers are unemployed, so the model saw this as an additional risk factor that further increased the likelihood of problems repaying the loan.

The one positive element was that you asked for a longer repayment period of 48 months. Longer durations tend to slightly improve the model's view of an application because the monthly burden is smaller. Unfortunately, this helpful effect was not large enough to overcome the concerns about your savings and employment.

You should focus on building verifiable savings and securing stable employment. Once those two areas improve, reapply. The bank will then see a meaningfully lower risk profile and your chances of approval should increase substantially.
